# Coverage matrix — 2026-09-19

**Which providers, in combination, make every value live.** Generated by
`npx tsx scripts/gen-coverage-matrix.ts` from two inputs, neither of which answers
the question alone: the source registry (`lib/data/dataSources.ts`), which knows
which providers *could* serve a surface and what each costs, and a live audit,
which knows what actually came back.

Audit: `http://localhost:3000` · mode **full** · run 2026-09-19T18:42:22.983Z
· 71 route probes (+6 cross-layer, which assert agreement
between layers rather than hitting a route) · registry: 51 surfaces

⚠ **IP-dependent.** The audit's verdicts depend on the egress it ran from, so this
matrix does too. Built from a cloud or CI run it describes that host, not a user.

## The number

| | |
|---|---|
| Surfaces in the registry | 51 |
| Live now, no key needed | **30** |
| Upstream throttled the audit — not a gap | 1 |
| Degraded — not serving the intended source | **13** |
| …of those, a key would fix | 9 |
| …of those, no key fixes | 4 |
| Not covered by any audit probe | 7 |
| Keyed provider entries behind them | 5 |
| **Accounts a user would open for full coverage** | **3** |

The account figure is a greedy set cover, so it is an **upper bound**. 2 of the
3 are forced — the only vendor that can serve some surface — and the
remainder were chosen most-surfaces-first. It counts accounts, not money: several have a
free tier, and the registry records `paid` separately from `key` for exactly that
reason. It also counts only what a key can buy — the unfixable rows below are a
product gap, and no number of accounts closes them.

## If we walk away from a vendor

Standing rule (owner, 2026-09-18): **decisions that cost money are deferred until
close to the end of production**, and the app is built so that no single provider is
load-bearing. This table is how that rule is checked. "Strands" is what would have
no remaining option at all if that vendor were dropped — the number to drive to zero.

| Vendor | Cost posture | Could serve | Strands if dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Alpha Vantage** | held — no decision to take | 4 | — none |
| **FMP** | held (free tier) · paid upgrade **deferred** | 7 | **2**: stock-universe, fund-holdings |
| **Finnhub** | held — no decision to take | 4 | — none |
| **LunarCrush** | free signup | 1 | — none |
| **Santiment** | free signup | 1 | — none |
| **Tiingo** | held — no decision to take | 4 | — none |
| **Twelve Data** | held — no decision to take | 4 | — none |
| **YouTube Data API** | free signup | 1 | **1**: videos |

### Single-sourced surfaces — the optionality risk

Exactly one vendor can serve each of these. They are where the rule is not yet
satisfied: dropping that vendor does not degrade the surface, it removes it.

- **Videos / video search** (`videos`) — only YouTube Data API (free signup)
- **Stock Registry universe** (`stock-universe`) — only FMP (held (free tier) · paid upgrade **deferred**)
- **ETF / fund holdings** (`fund-holdings`) — only FMP (held (free tier) · paid upgrade **deferred**)

### The ones no account closes

Every provider on these entries is keyless, and the keyless providers already ran
in this audit. So the gap is a geo-block, a withdrawn source, a terms decision or a
genuine absence — not a price. These are the rows that decide what "every value
live" can even mean.

- **Crypto OHLCV / candlestick charts** (`ohlcv`, FALLBACK) — providers: Binance (primary/none), Binance.US (fallback/none), CoinGecko (primary/none)
  - `/live-data/ohlcv?id=btc&range=1Y` → FALLBACK — 365 candles — Binance.com geo-blocked, served by Binance.US (different venue/prices)
  - `/live-data/ohlcv?id=xrp&range=6M` → FALLBACK — 180 candles via Binance.US
  - `/live-data/ohlcv?id=eth&range=MAX` → FALLBACK — 365 candles via Binance.US
  - registry note: Binance.com is 451 (geo-blocked) from many hosts, so candles come from the US mirror — a different venue. Serving venue recorded in the `venue` field.
- **Coin list / search / discovery** (`coin-list`, FAIL) — providers: CoinGecko (primary/none), Binance.US (fallback/none)
  - `/live-data/coin-search?q=bitcoin` → FAIL — HTTP 404, non-JSON body
- **Crypto price chart (legacy, internal)** (`chart`, FALLBACK) — providers: CoinGecko (primary/none)
  - `/live-data/chart?id=btc&days=30` → FALLBACK — 721 price points, correctly marked synthetic:true (not real OHLC)
  - registry note: Synthesises zero-range OHLC from a price-only series (marked synthetic:true). No app consumers — /live-data/ohlcv provides real candles.
- **Equity screener / outliers** (`stock-outliers`, FALLBACK) — providers: Derived from stock-universe (derived/none)
  - `/live-data/stock-outliers?min_mcap=2` → FALLBACK — only 66 evaluated across 7 sectors — screening the curated catalog, not the real universe
  - registry note: Sector z-scores over whatever universe stock-universe returns — inherits its narrowness on the catalog fallback.

## Throttled, not missing

Every failing probe on these surfaces was the upstream rate-limiting the audit —
a full run fires dozens of probes in minutes and several share one keyless
provider. They are excluded from the counts above and from the account cover,
because a paid plan is not the remedy for a surface that is already working.
**Re-probe before treating any of these as a gap.**

- **On-chain wallet balances (BTC/ETH/SOL/TRON/XRP + EVM)** (`wallet`, FAIL)
  - `/live-data/wallet/tron?address=TR7NHqjeKQxGTCi8q8ZY4pL8otSzgjLj6t` → FAIL — HTTP 502: Tronscan HTTP 429

## Registry surfaces no probe covered

Not a verdict — an absence of one. Either the audit has no test for the route, or
the entry's `route`/`covers` do not match any path the audit hits. Both are worth
knowing: an unprobed surface contributes nothing to the number above, so the
account count is computed over a smaller world than the registry describes.

- `coin-profile` — Coin project profile (website, description) (/live-data/coin-profile, status `live`)
- `global` — Global crypto aggregates (BTC dominance, total cap) (/live-data/global, status `live`)
- `withdraw-fees` — Live exchange withdrawal fees (Transfer Fee Calculator overlay) (/live-data/withdraw-fees, status `partial`)
- `ipo-calendar` — IPO calendar (/live-data/ipo-calendar, status `key-gated`)
- `futures-curve` — Futures term structure (forward curve) (/live-data/futures-curve, status `unavailable`)
- `brief` — AI Daily Brief (/api/agents/research, status `derived`)
- `options-score` — Trade Risk Scorer (options) (/api/v1/options/score, status `derived`)

## Probes that match no registry entry

The join's other direction, and usually a test outliving the route it tested. The
registry is regenerated when a route is cut; the audit's test list is hand-maintained,
so it is the half that goes stale — and a 404 from a route deleted on purpose reads
as a data failure to anyone scanning the summary. These contribute nothing to the
account count either way.

- 🟢 `/live-data/assets/list` (assets/list) → **REAL** — 75 assets (static catalog by design)
